The landlord told her orally that he was terminating the lease for unpaid rent, but she cannot say whether written notice was sent or received; she describes possible shared-mailbox and registered-letter delivery problems. result.answer: First establish promptly whether written notice or a registered-mail collection notice exists and when it was sent, delivered, or first known, to preserve any applicable deadline. Then obtain the checklist-listed documents before assessing form, service, dates, or arrears grounds.

reply.subject: Information and documents needed about the possible lease termination

clauses.text: You report that you fell behind on April and May rent after losing your job, have since paid part, and that Mr Zürcher told you orally that he was terminating the lease because of unpaid rent.
You also say you do not know whether written notice was sent and that letters or registered-letter notices may be lost or taken by other tenants.

Please tell us promptly whether you have since found or received any written termination or registered-mail collection notice, and when you first became aware of it; if available, please send the notice, its envelope, collection notice, and any delivery or tracking record.
Please send the lease contract and any document showing the agreed notice period and termination dates.
Please send any written notice or other document stating the termination reason, and any cure/payment-deadline letter that warned of termination.
Please send a rent account or ledger and evidence of rent payments, including the partial payment, so the amounts due and any outstanding balance can be checked.
Please also tell us whether the flat is your family home, whether you had previously raised tenant rights with the landlord, and whether you wish us to consider an extension of the tenancy.
Please forward any written correspondence with the landlord about the tenancy or the arrears.
